tagline: Up the Farmington River to the axe makers' village.
intro: From Perry Street in Farmington, Route 4 follows the Farmington River two miles west into Burlington, where Route 179 turns north up the river into Canton and crosses it at Collinsville.

Collinsville belonged to the Collins Company, the largest maker of axes in the 19th century. Its tools went into the Trans-Siberian Railway and the California Gold Rush, and Admiral Peary carried them to the North Pole. It was here, the historian Diana Muir writes, that Elisha Root, working for Samuel Collins, invented die casting.

moments.title: Route 179
moments.text: North of Route 4 the road heads up the Farmington into Canton and crosses the river at Collinsville.

moments.title: Collinsville
moments.text: The axe factory shut in 1966, but its buildings still ramble along the riverbank among a maze of sluices, rented now to local businesses.
